title: Week Summary: Context and Functional Viewpoints

concepts.name: Context viewpoint
concepts.description: A viewpoint focused on the system boundary, external actors, external systems, and environmental interactions.

concepts.name: Actor
concepts.description: A person, role, organization, or system that interacts with the system from outside its boundary.

concepts.name: External interface
concepts.description: A boundary where the system communicates with another system, person, device, or service.

concepts.name: Context diagram
concepts.description: A model showing the system of interest, external actors, external systems, and relationships among them.

concepts.name: Functional viewpoint
concepts.description: A viewpoint focused on functional elements, responsibilities, interfaces, and collaborations that deliver system behavior.

concepts.name: Functional element
concepts.description: A major runtime part of a system that owns a coherent functional responsibility.

concepts.name: Responsibility assignment
concepts.description: The allocation of behavior or capability to architectural elements.

concepts.name: Functional collaboration
concepts.description: The interaction among functional elements needed to complete a system behavior.

concepts.name: Functional cohesion
concepts.description: The degree to which responsibilities within an element belong together.

concepts.name: Functional coupling
concepts.description: The degree of dependency between functional elements.

concepts.name: Functional boundary
concepts.description: A division between responsibilities that affects ownership, change, interfaces, and runtime collaboration.

concepts.name: Responsibility leakage
concepts.description: A design problem where behavior crosses boundaries in ways that weaken cohesion or ownership.
